subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: Should Slack DM/main sessions receive privacy-scoped recall of the same agent's outbound channel messages, and what authorization, retention, edit/delete, and disclosure rules must govern that recall?
rationale: Source proves the blind spot, but choosing which channel content may cross into a DM is a product and security-boundary decision that cannot be inferred safely from existing session visibility settings.

options.title: Add a scoped activity ledger
options.body: Record and query only the agent's own outbound Slack activity with workspace, account, destination, authorization, retention, and deletion constraints.

options.title: Use broad same-agent visibility
options.body: Document `tools.sessions.visibility: "agent"` as the solution, accepting that it exposes complete same-agent sibling transcripts rather than only self-authored Slack activity.

options.title: Preserve session isolation
options.body: Decline automatic cross-session recall and document explicit memory or session-tool workflows as the supported boundary.

recommendation.title: Add a scoped activity ledger
recommendation.body: Record and query only the agent's own outbound Slack activity with workspace, account, destination, authorization, retention, and deletion constraints.

likelyOwner.reason: The public review and recent routing/outbound history make steipete the strongest available owner for the cross-session product and privacy decision.
